# Vendored crates

## edit-session

Document Properties uses the dependency-free draft state machine from
[edit-session 0.1.0-alpha.2](https://github.com/PerchAnton/edit-session/tree/033f7c3a67b825b8f222288788cc61234c0c945d).
The manifest, library, lifecycle tests and both licenses match that revision byte for byte.
The local README links here and rustfmt settings preserve upstream formatting. PdfCraft owns document identity, permissions and Undo.
Review upstream changes before replacing the snapshot and run the lifecycle and Document Properties tests.

## Window-stack provenance after the egui 0.37 migration

The checked-in, resolved Cargo graph pins `winit` to storytold/winit
`a517b3846ee8457d84ee4975110bfda6797c44dc` and the egui crates to storytold/egui
`725a39fca940f77149ffbb9c58eef405a16997bc`. Neither `vendor/winit` nor
`vendor/egui-wgpu` is a root `[patch.crates-io]` path entry. The retained copies
record the app's earlier patches; their source-reading tests establish provenance,
while the resolved forks and their behavioral tests establish runtime behavior.

The retained winit copy has upstream base `e9809ef54b18499bb4f2cac945719ecc2a61061b`,
as recorded in `vendor/winit/.cargo_vcs_info.json`. Its thirteen patch rows below
match the fork's `PATCHES.md` entries W1–W13 commit for commit (W1 `b357a332`,
W2 `13ca693b`, W3 `fd104a4c`, W4 `3fffb7ce`, W5 `283370ce`, W6 `a82b90fb`,
W7 `9b90d5bd`, W8 `6a87addd`, W9 `9500f25d`, W10 `4a7dd791`, W11 `4df8554b`,
W12 `7facf001`, W13 `5506b1a9`). The reviewed winit fork additionally carries
W14–W27 (W14 is opt-in and is not enabled by PdfCraft). `vendor/egui-wgpu` carries
E2 (`surface_fit`) and E3 (`catch_errors`); the egui-wgpu 0.37 fork retains both,
including its `surface_fit` tests exercised by PdfCraft's behavioral tests.

Keep both copies while their provenance tests remain in use. Renderer and security
vendors below retain their independent path patches and licenses.

Permissively licensed crates we carry small patches for. Each directory keeps the upstream
licence files unchanged. Every patch is marked `PdfCraft patch:` in the source, is covered by a
PdfCraft test, and should be proposed upstream. Remove the vendored copy once upstream releases
the fix. Vendoring copyleft code is never allowed (plan/adr/0001).

| Crate | Version | Licence | Patches | Test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| lopdf | 0.45.0 | MIT | (1) PNG predictor rows longer than the data are refused before their buffers are allocated (a fuzzed `/Columns 4294967295` allocated two 4 GiB rows), and empty frames return without row buffers; (2) predictor row widths use saturating arithmetic or reject overflow; (3) sub-byte TIFF Predictor 2 scratch is bounded by the samples present in the input instead of the declared `/Colors`, aligned with [lopdf#589](https://github.com/J-F-Liu/lopdf/pull/589); (4) the object lookup keeps its cycle history through compressed objects, requires an ordinary in-file container, and caps the chain of indirect lookups at 16 (a chain of new objects, each a `/Length` compressed in a container whose own `/Length` names the next, or a stream whose `/Length` names the next stream, overflowed the stack: a dev build's 2 MiB thread within 800 hops); (5) object-stream members are parsed within their own extent (up to the next distinct offset), an entry whose offset repeats an earlier entry's is skipped (so a repeated object number can resolve to its earlier entry), and offsets are processed in index order; (6) `find_latest_trailer`: a rebuild takes a `/Type /XRef` stream dictionary as the trailer when the file has no `trailer` keyword (the latest in the file wins, as a later `trailer` would), so a concatenated or truncated file keeps its /Info and /ID instead of failing to load; a candidate whose /Root is the catalog beats one whose /Root is another dictionary, and an in-file /Root must match its generation (#2365); (7) object parsing builds at most 4,194,304 objects (every array element and dictionary value at any depth, `parser::MAX_OBJECT_NODES`, the same cap as `pdfcraft_cos`) per top-level object, an object stream reads at most 1,000,000 index entries (cos's `/N` clamp), and one load builds at most 8,388,608 objects from all of its object streams together, shared across rayon workers (a decoded stream of `0 0 0 ...` inside the 256 MiB decompression limit built ~120M objects, 10+ GB, and aborted). A lookup parses only the member it wants, so it isn't skipped behind a large member, and a load parses only the members it would add: none its cross-reference table places in another stream (stale copies) and none already loaded as an ordinary object or from an earlier stream. Members the table doesn't list at all are still parsed (a rebuilt table lists no compressed objects) and share the budget, so they can spend it before listed members of the same stream; a load expands its object streams one at a time in object-number order, a stream's members in parallel only when the budget holds all of them and otherwise in index order, so a spent budget skips the same members on every load (#5083) | (1) `inspect::tests::png_predictor_rows_longer_than_the_data_are_refused_before_allocating`, `inspect::tests::empty_png_predictor_frames_do_not_allocate_rows`; (2) `inspect::tests::tiff_subbyte_predictor_row_width_overflow_is_refused`; (3) `inspect::tests::tiff_subbyte_predictor_scratch_is_bounded_by_available_samples`, `inspect::tests::tiff_subbyte_predictors_keep_components_rows_and_padding`; (4) `inspect::tests::compressed_object_self_container_does_not_recurse`, `inspect::tests::compressed_object_mutual_containers_do_not_recurse`, `inspect::tests::object_stream_length_cycle_does_not_recurse`, `inspect::tests::compressed_object_container_chain_does_not_recurse`, `inspect::tests::compressed_length_chain_does_not_recurse`, `inspect::tests::plain_stream_length_chain_does_not_recurse`, `inspect::tests::compressed_objects_and_indirect_stream_length_still_load`, `inspect::tests::compressed_length_in_a_container_with_an_indirect_length_still_loads`; (5) `inspect::tests::object_stream_member_extents_bound_owned_strings`, `inspect::tests::object_stream_member_extents_preserve_index_order_and_whitespace`; (6) `inspect::tests::rebuilt_file_keeps_the_info_of_its_cross_reference_stream`, `inspect::tests::rebuilt_file_prefers_a_trailer_whose_root_is_the_catalog`; (7) `inspect::tests::{object_stream_members_over_the_node_cap_are_skipped, object_stream_index_entries_past_the_clamp_are_ignored, object_streams_of_one_load_share_their_node_budget, object_streams_loaded_in_parallel_share_their_node_budget, a_malformed_object_stream_member_refunds_its_reservation, a_tight_budget_builds_object_stream_members_in_index_order, a_lookup_in_an_object_stream_parses_only_the_member_it_wants}` (pdfcraft-render; `NodeBudget` and `ObjectStream::new_within` are public so these can use a small budget) |
| winit | 0.30.13 | Apache-2.0 | (1) on Windows 11 (build 22000 and later), `WM_DPICHANGED` applies the rect Windows suggests. It used to nudge the window onto the monitor `MonitorFromWindow` names, which during a drag is still the monitor being left; the nudge sent another `WM_DPICHANGED`, so a window dragged to a monitor with another scale factor grew and stayed on the wrong monitor at the wrong scale (#324). Backport of winit master 488c036a ([winit#4341](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4341)), which no 0.30 release has; Windows 10 keeps the old adjustment, as on winit master. (2) on Wayland, a seat's text input is destroyed when the seat goes away, not whenever it loses a capability: losing any capability (a touch screen or tablet unplugged, a remote-desktop session ending) destroyed it, and only an added capability recreated it, so IME stopped working until restart. Port of [winit#4747](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4747); (3) on Windows, an IME composition reports its cursor from `GCS_CURSORPOS` only when `WM_IME_COMPOSITION` says it is set, and at the end of the composition otherwise: the Microsoft Korean IME never sets it, so the cursor read as 0 (egui then drew no caret while composing; it now draws it after the syllable). Port of [winit#4746](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4746); (4) on Windows, a hidden window is not maximized until it is shown, and a hidden window shown while maximized gets one `ShowWindow(SW_MAXIMIZE)`: `SW_MAXIMIZE` shows a hidden window, so PdfCraft, which eframe keeps hidden until its first frame is drawn, appeared unpainted (white) when it restored a maximized window, and could lose its focus. Port of [winit#4587](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4587) (the later, focus-safe form of [winit#4575](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4575)); (5) on X11, when allowing or disallowing IME replaces the focused window's input context (egui does it each time a text field gains or loses focus), the new context is focused: no focus event follows, so it stayed unfocused until the window lost and regained focus. Port of [winit#4727](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4727); (6) on macOS, `insertText` commits through IME when a composition was started (`pending_commit`, set by `setMarkedText`) rather than when marked text is left: input methods that end a composition with `unmarkText` before `insertText` lost the text, and Apple Korean dropped the key typed after a syllable (`한` then `5` or `;`); other `insertText` calls stay `KeyboardInput`; a commit outside a key press (a candidate clicked with the mouse, dictation) clears the marked text and leaves no key to swallow, as in [winit#4748](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4748) (without it the next key, such as Backspace, was lost). `validAttributesForMarkedText` lists the underline and marked-clause attributes, without which some input methods don't compose. Port of [winit#4650](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4650), the 0.30 backport of [winit#4651](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4651) (merged on winit master), with the underline attribute spelled as AppKit's `NSUnderlineStyleAttributeName` (`NSUnderline`); (7) on macOS, disallowing IME with a composition in progress (focus leaving a text field) tells the input method to discard its marked text (`discardMarkedText`): it kept composing it once IME was allowed again, so the abandoned syllable came back (`하`, then `가` typed in the next field, became `학`, then `하` + `가`; Japanese `か` then `さ` became `傘`). Port of [winit#4745](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4745); (8) on macOS, text inserted outside a key press without a composition (the emoji picker) is reported as `Ime::Commit`; it was dropped. Port of the emoji-picker part of [winit#4749](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4749) (0.30 backport of [winit#4748](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4748)); its `selectedRange` change for dictation is left out because it switches on press-and-hold for every held key (an accent menu instead of key repeat, and the chosen accent added after the repeated letters); (9) on macOS, a key whose text was committed through IME isn't also sent as `KeyboardInput` unless AppKit forwards it as a command (Enter): Apple Korean answers Space with no syllable in progress with `setMarkedText(" ")`, `insertText(" ")`, `setMarkedText("")`, and the last call reset winit's state, so the space arrived twice. Same goal as [winit#4478](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4478), whose changes don't reach this call order (macOS 14); to be proposed upstream there; (10) on macOS, when the first key in a fresh app reaches Apple Korean's `insertText` as a raw compatibility jamo instead of starting a composition, that key is interpreted once more, synchronously, before it is sent as `KeyboardInput` (g k s typed ㅎㅏㄴ instead of 한); only an unmodified, non-repeated first key whose one callback inserts that same jamo, with IME enabled and nothing composed, focus and input source unchanged, is retried (`ime_startup.rs`). Port of [winit#4744](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4744), with its policy tests.; (11) on X11 without `Xft.dpi`, the scale factor comes from the X screen's configured DPI (its size in pixels and millimetres) before the output's physical density from RandR: Xorg can deliberately run a dense panel at 96 DPI, and only winit applications then looked zoomed; `Xft.dpi` still wins, `WINIT_X11_SCALE_FACTOR` still overrides, and a screen reporting no size keeps the RandR fallback. PdfCraft patch (#1150, replacing the launcher pin proposed in #908). (12) on macOS, `WinitView` answers `mouseDownCanMoveWindow` with the window's `movable_by_window_background` attribute (NO unless asked): NSView answers YES for a view that isn't opaque, so with the transparent title bar and full-size content view PdfCraft uses, AppKit moved the window for any drag that began in the 28 pt title-bar band before the app saw it, and document tabs (which live in that band) could not be dragged to reorder them. The empty strip still moves the window through `ViewportCommand::StartDrag`. PdfCraft patch. The published crate's asset files (`docs/res/*.svg`, `examples/data/*.png`) are left out, so its `window` example doesn't build; (13) on Wayland, pixel-only wheel, wheel-tilt and continuous-source scroll events report `Moved` rather than starting an unterminated finger gesture, so egui follows modifier release instead of keeping Ctrl zoom latched (#991). Finger gestures and unknown sources retain their existing phase policy | (1) `pdfcraft` `tests::winit_carries_the_windows_11_monitor_scale_fix` keeps the patch in the build; the drag itself needs two monitors with different scale factors on Windows 11; (2) `pdfcraft` `tests/winit_wayland_text_input.rs`; the capability change itself needs a Wayland session and an input method; (3) `pdfcraft` `tests/winit_windows_ime_cursor.rs`; composing itself needs the Microsoft Korean IME; (4) `pdfcraft` `tests/winit_windows_hidden_maximized.rs`; the start-up itself needs Windows and a window that was closed maximized; (5) `pdfcraft` `tests/winit_x11_ime_focus.rs`; switching fields itself needs an X11 session and an input method (IBus, fcitx5); (6) `pdfcraft` `tests/winit_macos_ime_commit.rs`; composing itself needs macOS and an input method; (7) `pdfcraft` `tests/winit_macos_ime_discard.rs`; composing itself needs macOS and an input method; (8) `pdfcraft` `tests/winit_macos_emoji_picker.rs`; the picker itself needs macOS; (9) `pdfcraft` `tests/winit_macos_korean_space.rs`; composing itself needs macOS and Apple Korean; (10) `pdfcraft` `tests/winit_macos_korean_first_key.rs` and `ime_startup.rs`'s own tests (run them with `rustc --test`); typing itself needs macOS and Apple Korean; (11) `pdfcraft` `tests/winit_x11_dpi.rs` keeps the patch in the build, and `util::randr` tests the policy (run them in the vendored crate); the scale itself needs an X11 session; (12) `pdfcraft` `tests/winit_macos_title_bar_drag.rs` keeps the patch in the build; the drag itself needs macOS and a pointer; (13) `pdfcraft` `tests/winit_wayland_scroll.rs` compiles the production phase policy and exercises modifier release through egui; live COSMIC confirmation remains open |
| egui-wgpu | 0.36.2 | MIT OR Apache-2.0 | (1) `winit::surface_fit`: a window's surface is configured within the device's `max_texture_dimension_2d`, both sides shrunk by one factor that egui then draws at (`pixels_per_point × render_scale`), so the whole window is drawn into the surface (on DX12 it is stretched over the window and lines up with the pointer; wgpu's GL backend copies it unscaled into a corner); the longer side becomes exactly the limit; the depth and MSAA textures follow, and a recreated surface starts again from the window's own size. egui-wgpu configured the window's size as is, and `Surface::configure` panics beyond the limit: a window restored at another monitor's scale (opening an Outlook attachment on a mixed-DPI laptop asked an 8192-pixel device for 8600 × 3423, #577) or stretched across monitors closed PdfCraft, before its window appeared when it happened at start-up ([emilk/egui#8361](https://github.com/emilk/egui/issues/8361)). The published crate leaves out egui's licence files; `LICENSE-APACHE` and `LICENSE-MIT` are from the 0.36.2 tag; (2) `winit::catch_errors`: a new window's surface is configured inside wgpu error scopes (validation, out of memory, internal), and a failure is returned as `WgpuError::ConfigureSurface` (for the root window at start-up eframe returns it as `Error::Wgpu`, which PdfCraft retries with OpenGL); nothing is kept for the window. wgpu's default handler panicked instead, and eframe configures the root surface before the app is created, so a driver that can't configure one closed PdfCraft at launch (a 2015 Intel GPU through wgpu's GL backend timed out waiting for the GPU to go idle, `GpuWaitTimeout`, #519). Unchanged, so still a panic: an error in a later reconfigure (resize, a lost surface), a device lost during the first configure (wgpu reports it only to a callback), and a window shown at zero size (first configured on resize) | (1) `pdfcraft` `tests::a_window_larger_than_the_gpu_limit_gets_a_surface_within_it`, `tests::surface_fit_never_empties_or_overflows_a_surface`, and `tests::vendor_provenance_egui_wgpu_surface_fit_identity`, which keeps the patch in the build and in the paths that size a surface; (2) `pdfcraft` `tests::a_gpu_error_while_a_window_is_set_up_is_returned_not_a_panic` (a real device: an error inside `catch_errors` is returned, not a panic) and `tests::vendor_provenance_egui_wgpu_catch_errors_identity`, which keeps it around `add_surface`'s configure |
| vello_common | 0.0.8 | Apache-2.0 OR MIT | (1) `clip::intersect` (the clip step every clipped path passes through) starts its row walk at the first row both paths have strips in, not the earlier of the two first rows. The walk visited every row from the top of the clip for each path (on the A1 sample's full-page canvas, about half its strip rows per stroke), and rows where one path has no strips produce no output, so the strips are unchanged (vello_common 0.1 starts at the later row too). Its cost grew with the page, and a full-page render of the A1 sample was about 30% faster; the output is byte-identical; (2) `StripStorage::room_for_path{,_within}`: whether one more path's coverage (at most the whole surface, counted twice) still fits below 2^31 values, the most a strip's packed alpha index reaches (`Strip::new` asserts it), or below a smaller limit; (4) `flatten::stroke`: when kurbo 0.13.1's stroker returns an outline containing NaN, which `fill` would drop whole, the path is stroked again from a copy (`robust_for_stroking`, one element out per element in) in which each curve whose control points lie within the stroke tolerance of its chord is a line (the #4907 fix, a nearly straight cubic given a NaN join, kurbo issues #617 and #519; its row here was lost in a merge and is restored with this entry) and each cubic whose second control point is its end point, as `y` builds (ISO 32000-2 §8.5.2.1 Table 58), has that control point moved the tolerance towards its first (`open_zero_end_handle`; the curve moves by at most 4/9 of the tolerance): kurbo's cusp search on such a curve's offset can stop on the end point, where the derivative is zero, and normalising it gives NaN, so at 16, 32 and 63 pt a two-curve `y` path drew nothing and a file in the PDFBox tracker lost its 32 pt "XX" outline. Only an exact zero triggers it (none of 192,000 random strokes with a handle 1e-9 long, nor of 256,000 `v` strokes, came back with NaN; 1,073 of 192,000 random `y`/`v` strokes at 1–64 pt did before and none after). A finite outline takes the old path unchanged | (1) `clip::tests::intersect_walks_only_rows_both_paths_have_strips` counts the rows the walk visits (`cargo test --manifest-path vendor/vello_common/Cargo.toml`) and fails without the patch; the render crate's pixel tests run through the patched crate; (2) `strip_generator::pdfcraft_tests::strips_have_room_until_a_surface_short_of_the_limit`; (4) `flatten::tests::a_tiny_degenerate_cubic_does_not_drop_the_stroke` and the render crate's `stroke_degenerate_cubic` fail without the near-line replacement, `flatten::tests::a_wide_stroke_of_a_curve_with_a_zero_end_tangent_is_drawn` (widths 1–64, every join and cap, `y` and the mirrored `v`) and the render crate's `stroke_zero_end_tangent` fail without the moved control point; `a_finite_outline_is_stroked_as_before` and `a_path_with_nan_is_still_dropped` pass either way |
| vello_cpu | 0.0.8 | Apache-2.0 OR MIT | (1) the single-threaded dispatcher leaves out a fill, stroke, fast rectangle or layer clip once the scene has no room for one more path's coverage (`StripStorage::room_for_path_within`, vello_common patch 2), records it (`RenderContext::coverage_full`, cleared by `reset`) and can be kept to fewer values (`RenderContext::set_max_coverage`, kept across `reset`). Every path's coverage stays in one buffer until the scene is rasterized, so a page that painted one form 2^22 times over (PDFBOX-5415) grew it past 2^31 values at about 7 GB and panicked in `Strip::new` (`alpha_idx` too large); it now renders what fitted. The multi-threaded dispatcher is unchanged (PdfCraft renders single-threaded); the backport of linebender/vello#2000 is recorded under the KenM76 integration patches (#5199) | (1) `raster::tests::coverage_budget::a_page_past_its_coverage_leaves_the_rest_out_and_says_so` renders a page that fills a circle 2^10 times with the rasterizer kept to 200,000 values, and fails without the dispatcher's check; `strokes_past_the_coverage_are_left_out`, `fast_rectangles_past_the_coverage_are_left_out` and `layer_clips_past_the_coverage_are_left_out` (the last through `RenderContext` directly, as hayro pushes no clipped layers, with the first clip kept below the limit and its pixels checked) each fail without that path's check, and `a_layer_clip_past_the_coverage_is_itself_left_out` fails when the clip is generated without room; vello_cpu's own tests need upstream assets that are not vendored |

Renderer startup errors: `egui-wgpu::RenderState::create` also wraps `Renderer::new` in
`winit::catch_errors` when the winit feature is enabled. A rejected shader or render pipeline
is returned as `WgpuError::CreateRenderer`, allowing PdfCraft's existing startup OpenGL retry.
The regression `pdfcraft` `tests::pipeline_creation_error_is_returned_and_device_remains_usable`
uses an invalid three-sample pipeline, then valid and invalid pipelines again on the same device.
Later rendering errors, device loss, and non-winit renderer construction are unchanged.

Temporary: lopdf is the bootstrap inspector (ADR-0004); M2.6 replaces it with `cos`/`model`.
